newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - GRE rules out buyback, profits slip.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - GRE rules out buyback, profits slip.

text.p: Britain's Guardian Royal Exchange Plc on Wednesday blamed tough competition and the continued strength of sterling for a sharp fall in trading profits in the first half of 1997.
The composite insurer also rejected recent calls by shareholders to use excess capital to buy back its shares in the near future.
Instead it would look to grow its businesses by selective acquisitions, said finance director James Morley, who stressed that a sizeable acquisition was not imminent.
Morley was speaking as GRE reported a 32 million pound ($52.2 million) fall in first half trading profits to 105 million pounds.
Sterling accounted for 9-1/2 million pounds of the decline.
Including investment income, pre-tax profits jumped to 502 million pounds from 231 million pounds and the net asset value per share rose 11 percent to 311 pence.
The dividend which is to be paid as a foreign income dividend to take advantage of advance corporation tax savings rose by 15 percent to 3.9 pence per share, above analyst expectations.

But with the exception of private motor, there were few signs of a rebound in premium rates and the company said it continued to face severe competitive pressures in all its main markets, particularly the UK.
Analysts said the underwriting performance was in line with expectations though investment income was slightly disappointing.
Worldwide general insurance premium income fell to 1,501 million pounds from 1,544 million pounds and underwriting losses to 64 million pounds from 51 million pounds.
GRE shares were down five pence at 290 pence.
Morley said the industry was experiencing a period of consolidation and opportunity for acquisition probably unrivalled in recent history.
"It doesn't seem to us to make sense to reduce the capacity of the company to make those acquisition at a time the availability of such acquisitions is so great," said Morley.
The company told analysts that it may review the question of a share buyback at the end of the full year.
GRE has targeted the life and health business as well as certain areas of its general business in the UK, Germany, Ireland and the U.S. for growth.
That could be achieved either organically or through acquisition, the latter only if suitable opportunities presented themselves, said Morley.
Analysts said the company is understood to be looking at a purchase in the U.S. for less than $100 million but that it had ruled out a UK life acquisition as too expensive.
The current trading environment continues to be difficult with competition across most markets intense.
GRE said household rates in the UK had shown very small increases this year but commercial property remained difficult.
However, motor rates had risen by around five percent so far this year with another five to 10 percent increase expected by GRE in the second half.
The U.S. performance was once again held back by storm and flood damage in the first three months of 1997.

Results in Britain were affected by an increase in frequency in private motor and higher subsidence claims. The group's direct operations, Guardian Direct and RAC Insurance Direct, continue to grow strongly with 778,000 policies in force at the end of June, up 15 percent on the year-end figure.
Direct opeartions now contribute 71 million pounds in premium income up from 28 million pounds last year. GRE said it would continue to grow the operation though not at the expense of margins.
Restructuring in the UK is on course to deliver the expected 27 million pounds of cost savings with 390 jobs now expected to go rather than the 350 originally envisaged.
($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
